requirements_summary:
Deployment: Private deployment in customer VPC (AWS-first). Prefer VPC peering / PrivateLink-style connectivity; no public internet egress from their app tier.
Data handling: customer-owned prompts/outputs; asked explicitly: "Do you store prompts or outputs by default?" (needs approved retention messaging).
Audit logging: must forward auth/admin actions + request metadata to Splunk; expects immutable trail for admin events (RBAC changes, key config changes, model/version rollouts).
Encryption: AES-256 at rest + TLS in transit; customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) required; key rotation at least annually; asked about HSM-backed keys (position as integration/option where applicable).
Identity: SSO/SAML required for Console; RBAC expectations: least privilege; separate roles for Platform vs Security.
Residency: US-only preferred; asked if any telemetry leaves region.
Performance: target workload is internal banker assistant + comms review; early target: p95 TTFT < 700ms and sustained throughput for ~50–100 concurrent users during peak; also asked about predictable per-token costs and ability to cap spend.
Model: wants access to at least two model options with fallback (policy-based routing).

notes:
ABM Pilot (FinServ) target. Strong fit for Hosted → Dedicated → Private story, but they will skip Hosted and go straight to Private/VPC evaluation if we can clear security fast.

Discovery notes (01/09):
- Current state: mix of internal GPU cluster (prototype) + exploring hyperscaler managed endpoints; security uncomfortable with public endpoints for regulated use-cases.
- Use-cases in scope:
  1) Banker assistant (internal) with tool calls into knowledge base + policy docs
  2) Comms review for outbound client messages (needs auditability)
  3) Summarization for call notes (they claim they can tokenize/redact for POC but vendor risk still required)
- "Predictability matters more than absolute best model." They want consistent latency + ability to isolate workload.
- Key buying criterion: deployment boundary clarity + evidence package. Dana (Security): "If we can’t explain where data flows and who has access, we can’t move."

Security requirements (high confidence):
- SOC2: required; share report under NDA.
- Audit logs: must be exportable to their SIEM; need admin + access logs. They asked about retention controls for logs and whether they can set retention to 0 for prompts/outputs.
- KMS: customer-managed keys required (AWS KMS). Asked about HSM-backed keys; do not over-promise—provide accurate supported integrations and roadmap-safe language.
- SSO/SAML + RBAC: required for Console/admin access.
- Residency: US-only; clarify that Private/VPC keeps inference traffic within their VPC boundary; confirm any control plane metadata + where it resides.

Technical/deployment constraints:
- Network: VPC peering preferred; their platform team will not allow inbound from public internet to app tier.
- Egress: minimized; if any egress needed (updates/telemetry), must be allowlisted + documented.
- Logging: needs clear schema + sample events; wants fields for who/what/when on model version changes, policy updates, admin actions.

Open questions to close in deep dive:
- Which AWS region(s) are mandatory? (They mentioned us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 DR as a maybe.)
- SIEM export format: Splunk HEC vs S3 + forwarder; batch vs streaming.
- Whether POC can run on masked data without full vendor risk signoff (Procurement suggests "no").
- Dedicated vs Private: Platform assumes Private only; we should position Dedicated as an interim for non-sensitive workloads if security allows, but don’t push.

Internal guidance / what to send:
- Use FinServ security FAQ addendum language for retention + audit logs.
- Provide Private/VPC reference architecture and highlight shared responsibility model.
- If they ask "Do you store prompts/outputs?" use approved residency/retention positioning doc; avoid blanket "we never store" statements.

Deal motion:
- Goal: book technical deep dive within ABM pilot window; then propose 2–3 week POC with explicit success criteria (latency, throughput, audit log export functioning, KMS integration validated).
- Likely next meeting attendees: Samir (Platform), Dana (Deputy CISO), Mei (Governance), Eric (ML Eng) + Fatima (SE) + Avery (AE) + optional Olga Petrov (GRC) if questionnaire heavy.

Risk:
- Competing internal effort: self-host vLLM on their GPU cluster; they believe they can meet requirements but admitted operational burden is high. Need to emphasize reliability, observability, routing/fallback, and cost/latency predictability in Private/VPC without making unsupported claims.

Customer quote (paraphrased): "We’re not looking for magic models; we need a serving layer we can defend in an audit."
